To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

dimethyl dihydrocaridines are presented as organic photocatalysts that enable the controlled polymerization of diverse acrylate-based monomers via organocatalyze atom transfer radical polymerizations.

dimethyl dihydro acridines are presented for the first time as photocatalysts for the controlled polymerization of acrylate monomer, and that the properties of these photocatalysts are tuned through structural modification, enabling access to a diverse range of photocatalysts for this application.
dimethyl dihydroacidines are presented as photocatalysts for the first time in the organocatalyze atom transfer radical polymerisation of acrylate monomer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of novel photocatalysts for organocatalyze atom transfer radical polymerizations.
the development of new organic photocatalysts (OPCs) for the atom transfer radical polymerizations (ATRP) of challenging acrylates.

the development of novel photocatalysts for the atom transfer radical polymerizations of acrylate monomer, including structure-property relationships, the development of a continuous flow reactor, and the synthesis of well-defined block copolymers
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the development of a new family of PCs has enabled controlled polymerization of diverse acrylate-based monomers, which has not been possible using previously developed photocatalysts.
this thesis has demonstrated the utility of dimethyl dihydro acridines as photocatalysts for organocatalyed ATRP of acrylate monmers in a continuous flow system.

dimethyl dihydroacidines are presented for the first time as a new family organic PCs that enable the controlled polymerization of acrylate monomer via O ATRR, demonstrating tunable properties and accessing a strong oxidizing 2 PC* intermediate for efficient radical deactivation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dimethyl dihydrocaridines are an excellent class of photocatalysts, enabling the first controlled polymerization of acrylate monomer via O ATRPs.
the development of new photocatalysts has been essential to advancing organocatalyed atom transfer radical polymerizations, allowing access to challenging acrylate polymeric architectures.

dimethyl dihydrocaridines are an important addition to the family of organic photocatalysts, and that this new family of PCs can be used for O ATRP of challenging acrylates in continuous flow reactors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dimethyl dihydroacidines are a new family of PCs that are capable of efficiently deactivating radicals in the polymerization of acrylate monomer, which is a significant advance in photocatalysis.

the use of dimethyl dihydrocaridine based photocatalysts in combination with continuous flow reactors and LiBr addition enables the controlled radical polymerization of a wide variety of acrylate monomer, which is a challenging task in conventional O ATRP systems
